2608.01575.title: Measuring in-context algorithmic reasoning in language models against an exact Bayes-optimal standard
2608.01575.paper_summary: Whether large language models perform genuine algorithmic reasoning or mere pattern completion is hard to test, because most benchmarks lack a ground truth for correct inductive inference. We introduce F-ICL, an in-context-learning benchmark that supplies one exactly. Using the Turing-complete machine F, complement-symmetrised into sF to remove output-polarity bias, we exhaustively enumerate all 1.5 billion programs of length $L\le13$ and compute the Bayes-optimal posterior in closed form under a bounded universal (Levin--Solomonoff) prior; models are scored by how closely their served distributions approach it at matched evidence. Each task is paired with its bitwise complement, on which the optimum scores identically, so an original-twin gap isolates the model's inductive bias. Across 105 serving configurations spanning 37 open models (0.8B--675B) and frontier systems from four laboratories, models answer up to 92\% of queries correctly, yet 45 of 46 models yield distributions farther from the optimum than a keystroke reference, and their behaviour is bracketed by low-order prefix statistics fitted only on visible evidence. That reference is itself an algorithmic mixture, induced by a print-only machine with no loops, so the panel's implied measure sits closer to a loop-free mixture than to the loop-bearing optimum, independently of the reference machine. Updating is also non-monotone, which no prior explains: a Bayes-rational solved set can only grow in this realisable, noiseless setting, yet added examples produce $6{,}545$ solved-to-unsolved transitions against $13{,}702$ gains. The gap is not predicted by accuracy (Spearman $ρ=-0.19$, $p=0.21$), does not close with scale or across frontier generations in the serving modes that expose distributions, and is widened by instruction and reasoning post-training. F-ICL is released as an open, reproducible benchmark and toolkit.
2608.01575.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型是否進行真正的算法推理或僅僅是模式補全很難測試，因為大多數基準缺乏正確歸納推理的基準真相。<lb/>我們介紹了 F-ICL，一個提供準確基準的上下文學習基準。<lb/>使用圖靈完備的機器 F，經過補充對稱化為 sF 以消除輸出極性偏見，我們徹底列舉了所有長度為 $L\le13$ 的 15 億個程序，並在有界的通用（Levin--Solomonoff）先驗下以封閉形式計算貝葉斯最優後驗；模型的得分取決於其提供的分佈與匹配證據的接近程度。<lb/>每個任務都與其按位補數配對，其最優得分相同，因此原始-雙胞胎差距能夠隔離模型的歸納偏見。<lb/>在涵蓋 37 個開放模型（0.8B--675B）和來自四個實驗室的前沿系統的 105 種服務配置中，模型正確回答高達 92\% 的查詢，但 46 個模型中的 45 個所產生的分佈距離最優解更遠，且其行為受到僅在可見證據上擬合的低階前綴統計的限制。<lb/>該參考本身是一種算法混合，由一個無循環的僅打印機器誘導，因此小組的隱含測量更接近於無循環混合，而非具有循環的最優解，與參考機器無關。<lb/>更新也是非單調的，這一點沒有先前的研究解釋：在這個可實現的、無噪聲的環境中，貝葉斯理性解集只能增長，但添加的示例卻產生了 $6{,}545$ 個已解決到未解決的轉換，而獲得的數量為 $13{,}702$。<lb/>這一差距並不由準確性預測（Spearman $ρ=-0.19$, $p=0.21$），在揭示分佈的服務模式中不會隨著規模或前沿世代的變化而縮小，並且在訓練後的指令和推理中擴大。<lb/>F-ICL 作為一個開放的、可重複的基準和工具包發布。
